sections.html:
Staunton is an independent city in the Shenandoah Valley, between the Blue Ridge and Allegheny mountains, at an elevation of about 1,417 feet. It covers just under 20 square miles and is drained by Lewis Creek, which flows to the Middle River and on toward the Chesapeake Bay.

The city is a principal city of the Staunton-Stuarts Draft metropolitan area, which had 125,433 people in 2020. Augusta County surrounds it, and the county government offices are in Verona, next door.

Interstate 81 and Interstate 64 both pass just outside the city limits. Inside the city, the main roads are US 11, US 250 and State Route 262, which forms a limited-access beltway around the edge.

sections.h2: What is Staunton's history, and why does it show up in the houses?
sections.html:
Staunton was founded in 1747 and named for Lady Rebecca Staunton, wife of the colony's lieutenant governor. It became an independent city in 1902 and, in 1908, hired what is described as the nation's first city manager.

The result is a city with a large stock of older buildings. The National Register of Historic Places lists the Beverley Historic District downtown, a house called The Oaks that dates to the 1840s, and a frame cottage called the Sears House built around 1860.

If you own a house of that age, expect buyers and inspectors to look closely at the roof, the foundation, old wiring and lead paint. Those are the repairs that most often slow a conventional sale in older Shenandoah Valley cities.

sections.h2: What do the 2020 census numbers say about Staunton housing?
sections.html:
Staunton had 12,316 housing units in 2020, and 7.6% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.9% and the rental vacancy rate was 4.7%.

Almost four in ten Staunton households are one person. Houses that lose their only occupant, whether to a move or a death, are a common reason owners look for a quick sale.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Staunton, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Staunton has a humid subtropical climate with four distinct seasons. NOAA normals for 1991 to 2020 show about 40.6 inches of rain a year and 21.6 inches of snow.

  • The average January low is 24.7 degrees Fahrenheit, so pipes, crawl spaces and old heating systems get a hard test every winter.
  • Snow falls on about nine days a year on average, mostly from December through March.
  • July highs average about 84 degrees, with a record high of 106, which stresses roofs and attic ventilation.
  • Rain falls on roughly 118 days a year, which shows up as damp basements, gutters and wood rot.

Buyers who inspect a Staunton house will usually check the same items: roof age, moisture in the basement, the heating system and drainage around the foundation.

sections.h2: What are the main neighborhoods and parks in Staunton?
sections.html:
Downtown Staunton centers on the Beverley Historic District, with Gypsy Hill Park and Betsy Bell and Mary Gray Wilderness Parks on the mountaintop. Gypsy Hill Park covers 214 acres and includes a golf course, a lake, a pool and ball fields.

A former state hospital campus is now The Villages at Staunton, a condominium complex. The state gave the original Western State property to the Staunton Industrial Authority in 2005, and the site was redeveloped after the old prison there closed in 2003.

Parks and a walkable center are selling points you can point to when a buyer asks about the area. The Waverly Hill house, designed in 1929 by architect William Bottomley, and the Stuart House show how varied the older housing can be.

sections.h2: Who are the big employers and schools in Staunton?
sections.html:
Mary Baldwin University, Staunton City Schools, the Virginia School for the Deaf and the Blind and Western State Hospital are among the largest employers listed in the city's financial reporting, according to a 2015 table that Wikipedia summarizes. Treat that list as dated and confirm current numbers with the city.

The city school district runs T. C. McSwain, A. R. Ware and Bessie Weller elementary schools, Shelburne Middle School, Staunton High School and the Dixon Educational Center. Stuart Hall School is a private option, and the American Shakespeare Center brings visitors downtown.

Large public and nonprofit employers give the city a steady base of workers, but they do not make a house that needs work easier to list.

sections.h2: How do you get around Staunton without a car?
sections.html:
Staunton has Amtrak service on the Cardinal line, with the station downtown. It is the closest Amtrak stop for Harrisonburg and Lexington, which gives the city a rail link that many Valley towns lack.

The city once ran its own bus system, Staunton Transit Service, but it was dissolved in 1989. Most residents rely on cars, and I-81 and I-64 carry through traffic around the city rather than through it.

  • US 11 Business follows a slower route through downtown than the main US 11 bypass.
  • State Route 261 is the better truck route along US 11 and US 250.
  • State Routes 252 and 254 lead to rural parts of Augusta County.

When a buyer asks about commuting, these routes are the facts you can give them. A house near the beltway or a downtown stop can be pitched differently from one on a back street.

sections.h2: What does it cost in taxes to sell a house in Staunton?
sections.html:
Virginia sets its deed taxes by statute, and they apply the same way in Staunton as elsewhere in the state. The recordation tax is 25 cents per $100 of the price or assessed value, whichever is greater, under section 58.1-801.

The grantor's tax is 50 cents per $500 under section 58.1-802, and the statute says the seller pays it unless the parties agree otherwise. Half of that tax goes to the state and half to the locality.

  • Ask your closing agent to show the proration of city taxes on the settlement statement.
  • Keep the deed's stated price accurate, because the clerk will not record a deed that omits it.

sections.h2: What should heirs know before selling a Staunton house?
sections.html:
Heirs and executors in Staunton often sell without the standard seller disclosure form, because the Residential Property Disclosure Act excludes transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate. The exclusions in section 55.1-702 also list transfers to a spouse or lineal relative.

That exclusion does not change the need for clear title. Before any closing, make sure the person signing has authority from the circuit court or the will, and ask the estate attorney what the file needs.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer make sense in Staunton?
sections.html:
A cash offer fits when the house needs work, the owner lives elsewhere or the calendar matters more than the last few thousand dollars. It does not fit every situation, and a listing may net more for a house in good condition.

Compare the offers in writing, and look at what you keep after repairs, taxes, agent fees and the months a listing can take.

faqs.a: No. Staunton is an independent city, separate from Augusta County, although Augusta County surrounds it and keeps its government offices in nearby Verona.

faqs.q: Do older Staunton houses sell differently?
faqs.a: Often they do. Buyers and lenders look hard at roofs, foundations, wiring and moisture in older houses, and repair requests can slow or end a conventional sale. A cash buyer usually takes the house as it is.

faqs.q: Who pays the grantor's tax on a Staunton sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays unless the parties agree that the buyer covers some or all of it. The tax is 50 cents per $500 of value under Virginia Code 58.1-802.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Staunton house that is in probate?
faqs.a: You can once the person selling has legal authority, such as an executor named in a will. Confirm the steps with the estate attorney before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Where do I find Staunton's real estate tax dates?
faqs.a: Contact the City of Staunton Treasurer or Commissioner of the Revenue.
